r: The young Durgabai **translated Gandhi's speech into Telugu**, collected **Rs 5,000** and arranged his meeting with **Devadasis and Muslim women**

Founded by **Durgabai** in **Madras, 1937** – women's education and welfare
**"Andhra Mahila"**, **"Iron Lady (of Andhra)"**; honorary doctorate from **Andhra University**
**First chairperson, Central Social Welfare Board (1953)**; CSWB later registered under **Section 25, Indian Companies Act 1956**

Eluru, wife of **Maganti Bapineedu**; **first Telugu woman to give all her jewellery to the Tilak Swaraj Fund** and **burn foreign goods**; first to **give up foreign cloth and wear khaddar** during Gandhi's visit
A **dancer (devadasi)** who gave her **entire property** to the fund and followed Gandhi – "as Amrapali followed the Buddha"
Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma, Unnava Lakshmibayamma – orators and organisers

Title **"Desabandhavi"**; **first Andhra woman jailed** (first in India: **Parvati Devi** of Punjab); national school **Sanatana Vidyalayam**, Rajahmundry; made salt at **Chollangi (6 April 1930)** → Nellore jail; **lathi charge at Peddapuram (Quit India, 1942)**
**First woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha** (Vedaranyam, 1930); **first woman graduate of Andhra**
Jailed in the Salt Satyagraha **with her six-month-old baby**
Salt Satyagraha in **Madras city**; Constituent Assembly
Presided over the **first Andhra Rashtra Mahila Mahasabha**
Arrested at **17** for **distributing pamphlets**, Quit India (Guntur)
